author: copilot
body:
Sortino had unmaintained dependencies (some now built into Node.js), used deprecated APIs, and contained several bugs. This modernizes the stack while keeping all functionality intact.

## Dependencies
- **Replaced** `httpdispatcher` + `opn` → `express@^5.2.1` + `open@^8.4.2`
- **Dropped** `underscore`, `os-homedir`, `readline` — all superseded by native Node.js
- **Added** `express-rate-limit@^8.3.1` to protect file-system-touching routes
- **Added** `engines: { node: ">=18" }`; removed deprecated `preferGlobal`

## Bug fixes
- `setting.source` typo in `POST /move` (missing `s`) caused a crash on directory-create path
- `moveFile` passed a callback to `fs.renameSync` — sync API ignores it, errors were silently swallowed
- Destination directory creation race/failure replaced with `fs.mkdirSync({ recursive: true })`
- Hardcoded `data:image/jpeg` MIME type for all formats; now uses a `MIME_TYPES` map for `.png`, `.gif`, `.webp`

## Security
- `escapeHtml()` applied to all user-controlled values (filenames, folder names, settings paths) interpolated into HTML — prevents XSS
- Rate limiting (300 req/min) on all routes that touch the filesystem

## Code modernisation
- `var` → `const`/`let` throughout
- `new Buffer()` + manual `fs.open`/`fs.read` chain → `fs.existsSync` / `fs.readFileSync`
- `path.join()` for all path construction
- Extracted `listImages()`, `nextImageTag()`, `renderSettings()` to eliminate duplication
- jQuery CDN bumped `3.0.0` → `3.7.1` with updated SRI hash
- All commented-out dead code removed

author: jimeh
body:
## Summary

Add full text editor theme support to Hubris's Monaco editor, replacing the
previous chrome-only coloring (no syntax highlighting) with proper VS Code
theme compatibility.

- **VS Code theme format support**: Parse and apply VS Code JSON theme files
  (colors + tokenColors) to Monaco, with JSONC parsing for extension themes
  that use comments and trailing commas
- **21 built-in themes**: 2 Hubris themes (light/dark derived from the UI
  palette) + 19 VS Code built-in themes (Dark Modern, Monokai, Solarized,
  etc.) resolved from include chains and embedded via `include_str!`
- **Custom theme import**: Upload VS Code `.json` theme files from the
  Editor settings panel
- **Extension discovery**: Scan locally installed VS Code-based editors
  (VS Code, Cursor, Windsurf, VSCodium, Insiders) for theme extensions,
  deduplicate across editors (highest version wins), show install/update
  status, and one-click import
- **Settings model**: New `editor` section in settings with independent
  `lightEditorTheme`/`darkEditorTheme` selection that follows the
  light/dark/auto color scheme mode
- **Editor settings UI**: New "Editor" section in the settings dialog with
  theme dropdowns, file import, and extension browser

### Backend

- `EditorSettings` / `EditorSettingsPatch` added to settings TOML model
- CRUD API at `/api/editor-themes` (list, get, upload, delete)
- Discovery API at `/api/editor-themes/discover` + `/api/editor-themes/import`
- JSONC parsing via `jsonc-parser` crate (handles comments, trailing commas)
  with direct serde deserialization — no intermediate string stripping
- Extension scanner with semver-based deduplication across editors
- Content comparison for accurate installed/differs status detection
- Error logging on all editor theme API error paths for debuggability

### Frontend

- VS Code → Monaco theme conversion (`editorTheme.ts`)
- `applyMonacoTheme` refactored to accept editor theme data with full
  syntax rules, with signature-based idempotent caching
- Settings store extended with async editor theme fetch lifecycle and
  localStorage caching for instant paint
- Editor settings component with theme selection, file import, and
  extension browser UI

### Tooling

- `scripts/download-vscode-themes.ts`: Downloads latest VS Code release
  tarball, resolves include chains, writes self-contained theme files
- `mise run download:vscode-themes` task for updating bundled themes

## Test plan

- [ ] `mise run check` passes (format, lint, type-check, clippy)
- [ ] `mise run test` passes (all frontend + backend tests)
- [ ] Open a file tab — syntax highlighting renders with the default theme
- [ ] Switch editor themes in Settings → Editor — colors change immediately
- [ ] Light/dark/auto mode correctly switches editor themes
- [ ] Import a custom VS Code theme JSON file — appears in dropdown
- [ ] Click "From Extensions" — discovers themes from installed editors
- [ ] Import an extension theme — shows as "Installed" on refresh
- [ ] Delete a custom theme — removed from dropdown, falls back to built-in

author: madmax983
body:
💡 **What**: Added an optimized `rename_into` method to `Relation` that consumes the relation and its tuples to rename attributes in-place.
🎯 **Why**: The standard `rename` method clones all inner `ScalarValue`s and keys when constructing new tuples. By consuming the source relation, we can reuse the existing heap allocations, reducing memory overhead and cloning costs. This perfectly aligns with our zero-cost abstraction goals.
📊 **Impact**: Reduces heap allocations significantly for large relations. Benchmarks show a 5-11% speedup for renaming 1,000-element relations with 5 attributes compared to standard `rename()`.
🔬 **Measurement**: Verified using `criterion` benchmarks added to `perf_bench.rs` and local `cargo test`.

body:
## Summary

Closes Phase 1 of #21. Adds CASSCF/CASCI support to `compute_molecular_integrals` and 12 new CAS molecules to the registry, enabling 40-58 qubit systems.

**Key changes:**
- `compute_molecular_integrals(..., cas=(nelecas, ncas), casci=False)` — new params
- `_compute_cas_integrals()` helper — CASSCF/CASCI with auto-fallback at >50M configs
- `nuclear_repulsion = e_core` (frozen-core), NOT `mol.energy_nuc()` — verified: N₂ CAS(10,8) e_core=-77.38 vs E_nuc=23.57
- Cr₂ factory with `fix_spin_(ss=0)` to enforce singlet (prevents septet convergence)
- Benzene CAS(6,15) via CASCI (ncas=15 auto-triggers CASCI)
- joblib cache bypassed for CAS integrals (CASSCF is non-deterministic)
- 12 new registry entries: N₂-CAS ×5, Cr₂ ×6, Benzene ×1

**Files changed (4):**
- `src/qvartools/hamiltonians/integrals.py` — `cas`/`casci` params + `_compute_cas_integrals`
- `src/qvartools/molecules/registry.py` — 3 factory functions + 12 registry entries
- `tests/test_hamiltonians/test_cas_integrals.py` — 19 tests (new)
- `tests/test_hamiltonians/test_cas_factories.py` — 10 tests (new)

## Test plan

- [x] 19 CAS integral tests (shapes, e_core, electron counts, CASCI fallback, cache bypass)
- [x] 10 factory/registry tests (completeness, is_cas flag, N₂-CAS creation)
- [x] `ruff check` + `ruff format` clean
- [x] 354 existing tests pass (no regression)
- [x] N₂ CAS(10,12) end-to-end: 24Q Hamiltonian created successfully (89s)

## Remaining Phases (separate PRs)

- Phase 2: Sparse diag path (remove 10K limit) — unblocks >10K basis experiments
- Phase 3: CAS-aware FCI + pipeline scripts — unblocks experiment scripts
- Phase 4: Parameter auto-scaling — accuracy tuning

author: madmax983
body:
This PR unignores and runs a test case `test_pool_generation_overflow_panic` to demonstrate an active Use-After-Free/Denial-of-Service vulnerability inside `ResourcePool`.

### 🧨 The Trigger
If an attacker or long-running system cycles handles exactly `u32::MAX` times on the *same* internal `Vec` slot, the `generation` counter wraps to `0` or `u32::MAX` leading to either a silent Use-After-Free bypass (when wrapped back to original), or a direct thread crash due to integer overflow panics in Rust's debug builds: `let new_gen = *generation + 1;`.

### 📉 The Stack Trace
```
thread 'render_api::handles::tests::test_pool_generation_overflow_panic' panicked at crates/abrash-render/src/render_api/handles.rs:319:31:
attempt to add with overflow
```

### 🧪 Reproduction
Run `cargo test test_pool_generation_overflow_panic` or use `ResourcePool::remove()` on an item whose generation was artifically incremented to `u32::MAX`.

### 😈 Comment
"You assumed your server would never cycle 4 billion items in a single slot. Time makes fools of us all."

---

author: pyup-bot
body:
This PR updates [chardet](https://pypi.org/project/chardet) from **4.0.0** to **7.4.0.post2**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.4.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Performance:**

- Switched to dense zlib-compressed model format (v2): models are now
  stored as contiguous ``memoryview`` slices of a single decompressed
  blob, eliminating per-model ``struct.unpack`` overhead. Cold start
  (import + first detect) dropped from ~75ms to ~13ms with mypyc.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `354 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/354>`_)

**Accuracy:**

- Accuracy improved from 98.6% to 99.3% (2499/2517 files) through
  a combination of training and scoring improvements:

  - Eliminated train/test data overlap by content-fingerprinting test
    suite articles and excluding them from training data
    (`351 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/351>`_)
  - Added MADLAD-400 and Wikipedia as supplemental training sources to
    fill gaps left by exclusion filtering
    (`351 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/351>`_)
  - Improved non-ASCII bigram scoring: high-byte bigrams are now
    preserved during training (instead of being crushed by global
    normalization), and weighted by per-bigram IDF so encoding-specific
    byte patterns contribute proportionally to how discriminative they
    are (`352 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/352>`_)
  - Added encoding-aware substitution filtering: character substitutions
    during training now only apply for characters the target encoding
    cannot represent
  - Increased training samples from 15K to 25K per language/encoding pair
    (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)

**Bug Fixes:**

- Added dedicated structural analyzers for CP932, CP949, and
  Big5-HKSCS: these superset encodings previously shared their base
  encoding's byte-range analyzer, missing extended ranges unique to each
  superset
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `353 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/353>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.3.0
   ```
   -------------------

**License:**

- **0BSD license** — the project license has been changed from MIT to
  `0BSD <https://opensource.org/license/0bsd>`_, a maximally permissive
  license with no attribution requirement. All prior 7.x releases
  should also be considered 0BSD licensed as of this release.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)

**Features:**

- Added ``mime_type`` field to detection results — identifies file types
  for both binary (via magic number matching) and text content. Returned
  in all ``detect()``, ``detect_all()``, and ``UniversalDetector`` results.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `350 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/350>`_)
- New ``pipeline/magic.py`` module detects 40+ binary file formats
  including images, audio/video, archives, documents, executables, and
  fonts. ZIP-based formats (XLSX, DOCX, JAR, APK, EPUB, wheel,
  OpenDocument) are distinguished by entry filenames.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `350 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/350>`_)

**Bug Fixes:**

- Fixed incorrect equivalence between UTF-16-LE and UTF-16-BE in
  accuracy testing — these are distinct encodings with different byte
  order, not interchangeable
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)

**Performance:**

- Added 4 new modules to mypyc compilation (orchestrator, confusion,
  magic, ascii), bringing the total to 11 compiled modules
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)
- Capped statistical scoring at 16 KB — bigram models converge quickly,
  so large files no longer score the full 200 KB. Worst-case detection
  time dropped from 62ms to 26ms with no accuracy loss.
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)
- Replaced ``dataclasses.replace()`` with direct ``DetectionResult``
  construction on hot paths, eliminating ~354k function calls per full
  test suite run
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)

**Build:**

- Added riscv64 to the mypyc wheel build matrix — prebuilt wheels are
  now published for RISC-V Linux alongside existing architectures
  (`Bruno Verachten <https://github.com/gounthar>`_,
  `348 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/348>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.2.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Features:**

- Added ``include_encodings`` and ``exclude_encodings`` parameters to
  :func:`~chardet.detect`, :func:`~chardet.detect_all`, and
  :class:`~chardet.UniversalDetector` — restrict or exclude specific
  encodings from the candidate set, with corresponding
  ``-i``/``--include-encodings`` and ``-x``/``--exclude-encodings``
  CLI flags
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `343 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/343>`_)
- Added ``no_match_encoding`` (default ``"cp1252"``) and
  ``empty_input_encoding`` (default ``"utf-8"``) parameters — control
  which encoding is returned when no candidate survives the pipeline or
  the input is empty, with corresponding CLI flags
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `343 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/343>`_)
- Added ``-l``/``--language`` flag to ``chardetect`` CLI — shows the
  detected language (ISO 639-1 code and English name) alongside the encoding
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `342 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/342>`_)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.1.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Features:**

- Added PEP 263 encoding declaration detection — `` -*- coding: ... -*-``
  and `` coding=...`` declarations on lines 1–2 of Python source files are
  now recognized with confidence 0.95
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `249 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/249>`_)
- Added ``chardet.universaldetector`` backward-compatibility stub so that
  ``from chardet.universaldetector import UniversalDetector`` works with a
  deprecation warning
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `341 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/341>`_)

**Fixes:**

- Fixed false UTF-7 detection of ASCII text containing ``++`` or ``+word``
  patterns
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_,
  `332 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/332>`_,
  `335 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/335>`_)
- Fixed 0.5s startup cost on first ``detect()`` call — model norms are now
  computed during loading instead of lazily iterating 21M entries
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `333 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/issues/333>`_,
  `336 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/336>`_)
- Fixed undocumented encoding name changes between chardet 5.x and 7.0 —
  ``detect()`` now returns chardet 5.x-compatible names by default
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude,
  `338 <https://github.com/chardet/chardet/pull/338>`_)
- Improved ISO-2022-JP family detection — recognizes ESC sequences for
  ISO-2022-JP-2004 (JIS X 0213) and ISO-2022-JP-EXT (JIS X 0201 Kana)
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)
- Fixed silent truncation of corrupt model data (``iter_unpack`` yielded
  fewer tuples instead of raising)
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_ via Claude)
- Fixed incorrect date in LICENSE
  (`Dan Blanchard <https://github.com/dan-blanchard>`_)

**Performance:**

- 5.5x faster first-detect time (~0.42s → ~0.075s) by computing m

## Summary

Complete macOS desktop client for Immich with a native Photos-style three-pane UI.

## Features

### Core Architecture
- Photos-style NavigationSplitView three-pane layout (sidebar, grid, detail)
- Progressive image loading (thumbnail → preview → original) with NSCache (512 MB / 2000 items)
- Keychain-backed credential persistence with auto sign-in

### Library & Navigation
- Timeline-sectioned photo grid with lazy loading
- Smart search with server-side query support
- Sidebar: Library, Favorites, Videos, Live Photos, Panoramas, Screenshots, Imports, Recently Deleted
- Collections view with albums, people, shared links, memories

### Photo Viewer
- Full-screen detail view with hero transitions
- Live Photo playback with force-touch peek
- Keyboard navigation (arrow keys, escape, space)
- Drag-to-dismiss gesture

## Summary

- Adds `countPagesBatch(paths)` to `SyncStorageBackend` and `StorageBackend` interfaces, with implementations in all 5 backends (SyncMemoryBackend, MemoryBackend, IdbBackend, OpfsBackend, PreloadBackend)
- Adds `COUNT_PAGES_BATCH` opcode (19) to the SAB protocol, with chunking support in `SabClient` and dispatch in `SabWorker`
- Refactors `restoreTree` to use a two-pass approach: first pass creates directories/symlinks and collects file entries, second pass batches all `countPages` queries in a single backend call — reducing O(n) synchronous SAB bridge round-trips to O(1) during mount/restore

This was the last remaining unbatched operation in the restore path (`listFiles` and `readMetas` were already batched). For a PGlite database with N files, this eliminates N-1 SAB round-trips at mount time.

The IDB implementation uses a single readonly transaction for all count queries. Recovery-path calls (`readPage`, `maxPageIndex`) remain individual since they only fire for crash-recovery edge cases.

author: 404setup
body:
🎯 **What:** The vulnerability fixed
Fixed a potential Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability via memory/thread exhaustion in `Varint21FrameDecoderMixin.java`. The `kreno$executor` was using `Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor()`, which is backed by an unbounded queue.

⚠️ **Risk:** The potential impact if left unfixed
A malicious actor could send a rapid stream of small or malformed packets (e.g., a "nullping" flood) to the server. Because the packet decoding thread operates quickly while offloading monitoring data to the unbounded queue, the queue would grow uncontrollably until the server exhausted its heap memory (OOM), crashing the Minecraft server entirely.

🛡️ **Solution:** How the fix addresses the vulnerability
Replaced the `Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor()` with a manually configured `ThreadPoolExecutor` backed by a fixed-size `ArrayBlockingQueue` (capacity of 1024). Additionally, configured the executor with a `DiscardPolicy`. Under normal load, behavior remains identical. Under severe attack, excess background monitoring logs are safely dropped, ensuring the server remains stable.

author: rsnodgrass
body:
## Summary

- **ox-a9y fixed**: `session start` now captures `StartOffset` (file byte offset) from the JSONL source file before recording begins, so pre-session content is excluded by offset rather than relying solely on timestamp filtering. Previously `StartOffset` was always 0 in production — it was tested in isolation but never wired up.
- **ox-az9 fixed**: `ox doctor --fix` now refreshes credentials before pushing via `pushLedger` (same path as session upload). Previously `fixLedgerBranchAhead` and `fixLedgerBranchDiverged` called `PushWithRetry` directly without `PrePush`, so stale PATs caused HTTP 403.
- **Local remote credential injection fixed**: `RefreshRemoteCredentials` was mangling `file://` and plain-path git remotes by injecting real server PATs into them. Added `isLocalRemote` early-exit guard and `endpointFromRemoteURL` helper for endpoint derivation.
- **ox-dia0 fixed**: `codedb` indexing now fails fast when the worktree directory no longer exists (e.g. Conductor deleted it), and `CheckFreshness` caps indexing at 2 hours. Previously go-git could iterate git history indefinitely against a deleted path — observed burning 134–198% CPU for 21+ hours. Also removed unnecessary `dataDir` cache reset in `UpdateProjectRoot` that caused repeated config re-resolution and log spam on repos with many active Conductor workspaces.

## Root causes

**ox-a9y:** The test for `StartOffset` manually set it via `UpdateRecordingStateForAgent` — it tested the mechanism worked, but not that `runSessionStart` set it. No production code path ever called `os.Stat(sessionFile)` to capture the offset at start time.

**ox-az9:** Doctor tests used real git repos (unauthenticated bare repos) where missing credential refresh is invisible. The tests validated push success but couldn't detect the missing `PrePush` hook.

**Local remote:** `RefreshRemoteCredentials` host-matching logic checked `remoteHost != "" && ...` — for local paths (no hostname), `remoteHost` was empty so the check never fired, and credentials were injected into the path.

**ox-dia0:** `Index()` passed the daemon's lifetime context directly to go-git. When a worktree was deleted mid-index, go-git continued reading git objects from the still-accessible gitdir indefinitely. `UpdateProjectRoot` also reset `m.dataDir` on every heartbeat, triggering repeated `config.LoadProjectContext` calls as Conductor workspaces cycled.

## Test plan

```
go test ./cmd/ox/ -run "TestStartRecording_StartOffset" -v
go test ./cmd/ox/ -run "TestFixLedgerBranchAhead_UsesPushLedger" -v
go test ./cmd/ox/ ./internal/gitserver/ ./internal/session/ -short
go test ./internal/daemon/ -run "TestIndex_DeletedProjectRoot_FailsFast" -v
```

- `TestStartRecording_StartOffsetPropagated` — StartOffset from opts is stored in recording state
- `TestStartRecording_StartOffsetZeroWhenNoSessionFile` — zero when no session file
- `TestFixLedgerBranchAhead_UsesPushLedger` — ahead push succeeds via pushLedger
- `TestIndex_DeletedProjectRoot_FailsFast` — Index returns error immediately when projectRoot is gone

## What should be tested going forward

- **ox-ozlv (P3)**: Codify policy: push-path tests must use `createBareAndClone` (real git). When mocks are unavoidable, assert `opts.PrePush != nil`. Document in `docs/ai/specs/go-conventions.md`.

author: phansen314
body:
## Summary

- **KSP type-parameter handling**: generated wrappers now preserve method-level bounds (`<T : Comparable<T>>`) and forward interface-level type parameters (`Repo<T>` → `RepoTraced<T>`). Implicit `kotlin.Any?` bounds are filtered out. `Dependencies` flipped to `aggregating=true`.
- **withContext scope check**: both overloads now guard with `if (e.scope !== this) throw e`, consistent with `rail{}`, `FailMappingRail`, `MappingRail`, and `ErrorMappingRail`.
- **`orFail(context: String)` → `orFailContext { }` lazy API**: context message is now a `() -> String` lambda — zero allocation on the Ok path. Renamed to avoid overload ambiguity with `orFail(mapError)` when `E = String`.
- **Doc fixes**: removed stale `toFailUnless` reference, documented `renderContext()` frame ordering, updated CLAUDE.md/README/design docs for new API.
- **Test coverage**: added tests for `flatten()`, `toResOr()`, `toFailIf()`, `contextMap()` null handling, failMapping mapper throwing inside `withContext`, foreign-scope `FailException`, non-interface `@TraceContext`, zero-param methods, bounded type params, and generic interfaces.

- [x] `./gradlew :result-kit-ksp:test` — all pass

author: leedohoun
body:
### Motivation
- Improve visibility into raw JSONL quality and provide a JSON report for corpus inspection. 
- Make ingestion more robust by detecting and rejecting low-quality or wrapper/error pages (especially DART) and to avoid polluting Layer2/BM25/vector data. 
- Provide an overwrite workflow that can remove previously indexed vector records for a theme when rebuilding a corpus. 

### Description
- Add a new CLI script `scripts/inspect_raw_quality.py` that inspects JSONL files/directories, infers sources, computes content-length statistics, detects placeholders/wrappers, and can emit a JSON report. 
- Enhance `scripts_rag_pipeline.py` to support `--update-mode overwrite` semantics by removing raw/corpora files and pruning vector store entries for documents that belong to the overwritten theme, using `make_document_id`, and include additional summary fields in the ingestion report. 
- Rework DART extraction in `src/ingestion/dart.py` to better decode various encodings, detect mojibake and wrapper/error pages, fetch viewer contents, compute quality metadata (e.g. `wrapper_text_detected`, `body_error_type`, `encoding_fixed`, `mojibake_detected`), and only mark `has_body` when a valid body is extracted. 
- Improve forum scraping in `src/ingestion/naver_forum.py` by separating list parsing and body extraction, adding body sanitization, returning `body_extracted` and `content_source` metadata, and enforcing a minimum body length for inclusion. 
- Improve news scraping in `src/ingestion/naver_news.py` by separating search candidate parsing and article detail fetching, extracting title/body more robustly, validating documents with minimum content length and placeholder checks, and logging skipped candidates. 
- Strengthen Layer2 building in `src/rag/raw_layer2_builder.py` by validating raw documents per source (`_is_valid_news_doc`, `_is_valid_forum_doc`, `_is_valid_dart_doc`), skipping invalid records (and reporting counts), and returning document-quality statistics (`raw_docs_count`, `skipped_invalid_count_by_source`, `built_records_count`, `final_records_count`) from `rebuild_theme`.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed as part of this change set.

author: delano
body:
#2727 

## Summary

Implements single-authentication-method override configuration to restrict login pages to a single auth method. When enabled, users see only the specified authentication form (password, email/magic-links, WebAuthn, or SSO), with other enabled methods hidden.

### Changes

**Backend (Ruby)**
- Added `SINGLE_AUTH_KEYS` constant to `AuthConfig` listing the four mutually-exclusive modes
- Implemented four new methods in `AuthConfig`:
  - `password_only_enabled?` - restricts to password authentication
  - `email_auth_only_enabled?` - restricts to magic links (requires email_auth enabled)
  - `webauthn_only_enabled?` - restricts to WebAuthn (requires webauthn enabled)
  - `active_single_auth_method` - returns the active override name or nil
- Added `single_auth_method_config` and `single_auth_method_valid?` private helpers to enforce mutual exclusivity (max one flag set)
- Updated `sso_only_enabled?` to use the new `single_auth_method` config section with fallback to legacy `sso_config`
- Added comprehensive unit tests covering all env var mappings, feature interactions, and mutual exclusivity logic

**Frontend (TypeScript)**
- Added four new functions to `features.ts`:
  - `isPasswordOnlyMode()`, `isEmailAuthOnlyMode()`, `isWebAuthnOnlyMode()` - check individual modes
  - `activeSingleAuthMethod()` - returns active mode name or null
- Extended `AuthFeatures` interface with `passwordOnly`, `emailAuthOnly`, `webauthnOnly` fields
- Updated `getAuthFeatures()` to include the new fields
- Added comprehensive unit tests for all new functions

**Configuration**
- Added `single_auth_method` section to `auth.defaults.yaml` with four boolean flags (all default to ENV-based values)
- Updated `auth.test.yaml` with the new section (all flags false)
- Updated `.env.reference` with documentation for the new ENV vars
- Updated `config_serializer.rb` to include new flags in bootstrap features

**Test Helpers**
- Extended `auth_mode_helpers.rb` mock to support the new single-auth-method methods

### Behavior

- **Mutual exclusivity**: If more than one flag is set, all return false (safe fallback to showing all enabled methods)
- **Feature guards**: `email_auth_only_enabled?` and `webauthn_only_enabled?` return false if their respective features are disabled
- **Mode guard**: All return false in simple mode
- **SSO compatibility**: `sso_only_enabled?` additionally requires at least one SSO provider configured

## Related Issues

#2727 

## Test Plan

Added 344 lines of comprehensive unit tests in `spec/unit/onetime/config/auth_config_spec.rb` covering:
- Mode detection and defaults
- Feature toggle env var mappings (default-ON and default-OFF patterns)
- Single-auth-method override behavior
- Mutual exclusivity enforcement
- `active_single_auth_method` return values
- `SINGLE_AUTH_KEYS` constant validation

Added 127 lines of TypeScript tests in `src/tests/utils/features.spec.ts` covering:
- Individual mode detection functions
- `activeSingleAuthMethod()` behavior and precedence
- Integration with `getAuthFeatures()`
- Undefined window handling

All tests pass; no manual testing required.

### Motivation
- Provide a deterministic, auditable confidence model for reconciled identities so operators can answer "why did we decide this?".
- Persist per-identity evidence and provenance pointers to keep source artifact references and make scoring reproducible and traceable.
- Keep changes conservative and focused on scoring/reconciliation persistence without broadening discovery or adding remediation.

### Description
- Implemented a weighted identity scoring model in `src/homeadmin/reconcile/workflow.py` that computes an identity confidence from evidence dimensions `mac_match`, `stable_hostname`, `repeated_ip_history`, `service_continuity`, and a `contradiction_penalty`, and clamps scores to `[0.0, 1.0]`.
- Built provenance aggregation (`source_observation_keys` and `raw_artifacts`) and attached the provenance, combined artifact pointers, and the computed `identity_confidence` to reconciled asset snapshots and identity records in `reconcile_assets`.
- Added persistence for per-identity evidence via a new migration `migrations/0002_identity_evidence.sql` creating `identity_evidence`, plus a storage accessor `upsert_identity_evidence` in `src/homeadmin/storage/db.py` and logic to write evidence rows for each identity during reconciliation.
- Updated tests in `tests/test_reconcile_workflow.py` and `tests/test_reconciliation.py` to verify high-confidence MAC merges, low-confidence IP-only merges, confidence drops for contradictory evidence, and snapshot provenance.

### Testing

author: jsm174
body:
## Problem

`BGFX_FRAME_FLUSH` was added to allow submitting render commands without presenting the backbuffer. The implementation in `bgfx.cpp` simply skips calling `flip()` when the flush flag is set. This works on D3D/Vulkan/GL where skipping the present has no side effects, but on Metal it causes a deadlock.

Metal's render path acquires a drawable from `CAMetalLayer::nextDrawable()` during `submit()`, and `flip()` is responsible for both presenting that drawable and committing the command buffer. When `flip()` is skipped, the command buffer is never committed and the drawable is never released back to the pool. Since `CAMetalLayer` has a pool of only 3 drawables, after a few flush frames `nextDrawable()` blocks waiting for a drawable that will never be returned.

## Fix

Add a virtual `flush()` method to `RendererContextI` with an empty default (no behavior change for D3D/Vulkan/GL). In `bgfx.cpp`, call `flush()` when the flush flag is set instead of doing nothing. Override `flush()` in the Metal renderer to release the drawable and commit the command buffer without calling `presentDrawable`. Metal recycles drawables once all references are dropped and any in-flight command buffer work completes, so the drawable is properly returned to the pool while preserving the intended flush semantics of not presenting to the screen.

`SamKirkland/FTP-Deploy-Action@v4.3.4` throws `Error: Server sent FIN packet unexpectedly` on HostGator because `basic-ftp` 5.0.2 mishandles the server closing the TLS connection after `QUIT` — which is standard behavior. Additionally, the prune step that strips `.map` files and large CSVs was running *after* the deploy, uploading those files unnecessarily.

## Changes

- **Upgrade action `@v4.3.4` → `@v4.3.5`**: updates `basic-ftp` 5.0.2 → 5.0.5, which tolerates the server-side FIN after `QUIT` instead of treating it as an error
- **Fix step order**: move "Prune generated maps & large CSVs" to run *before* the deploy step so those files are never uploaded to HostGator

author: copilot
body:
`cf-ddns.sh` used several bash-only constructs while carrying a `#!/bin/sh` shebang, making it fail under `ash` (Alpine, OpenWrt, BusyBox). This replaces all bash-isms with POSIX-compatible equivalents.

## Changes

- **`source` → `.`** — POSIX dot-sourcing for config file
- **`echo -e` → `printf`** — portable output in `log()`, `check_ip_change()`, `send_email()`, `update_dns_records()`, and `main()`
- **Bash arrays + `${!var}` → `eval`** — `check_variables()` replaces `local vars=(...)` / `${!var}` indirect expansion with an `eval`-based loop over a plain word list
- **`[[ =~ ]]` regex → `grep -q`** — also fixes invalid `${$zone_identifier_v4_file}` double-dollar references
- **`[[ $update == *"..."* ]]` → `case`** — glob match in `update_dns_records()`
- **`[[ A && B ]]` → `[ A ] && [ B ]`** — compound test in `main()`
- **`<<<` herestring → heredoc** — `IFS=' ' read -r zone_identifier record_identifier << EOF` in `main()`
- **`local var=$(cmd)` → separate declaration + assignment** — combined form suppresses exit codes in POSIX sh; split across two lines throughout

```sh
# Before (bash-only)
local vars=("auth_token" "zone_name" ...)
for var in "${vars[@]}"; do
    if [ -z "${!var}" ]; then ...

# After (POSIX)
for var in auth_token zone_name ...; do
    eval "val=\${$var}"
    if [ -z "$val" ]; then ...
```

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Problem

The script `cf-ddns.sh` currently uses several bash-only features that make it incompatible with `ash` (used on Alpine Linux, OpenWrt, BusyBox, etc.). The goal is to rewrite the script so it works correctly under **both ash and bash**.

## Current bash-only constructs to fix

| Line(s) | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| L11 | `source "$CONFIG_FILE"` — not POSIX | Replace with `. "$CONFIG_FILE"` |
| L20, L91, L147, L176, L182 | `echo -e "..."` — not portable | Replace with `printf` |
| L26–32 | `local vars=(...)` array + `${!var}` indirect reference | Replace with explicit per-variable `[ -z "$var" ]` checks using `eval` |
| L39, L44 | `[[ ... =~ ... ]]` regex match + `${$var}` invalid double-dollar reference | Replace with `echo ... \| grep -q` pattern match and fix variable names |
| L173 | `[[ $update == *"..."* ]]` glob match | Replace with `case "$update" in *...*)` |
| L194 | `[[ "$type" != "A" && "$type" != "AAAA" ]]` | Replace with `[ "$type" != "A" ] && [ "$type" != "AAAA" ]` |
| L207 | `<<< "..."` herestring | Replace with a heredoc: `IFS=' ' read -r a b << EOF\n$(cmd)\nEOF` |

## Expected result

- The shebang stays as `#!/bin/sh` (compatible with both ash and bash when invoked correctly)
- All bash-specific syntax is replaced with POSIX-compatible equivalents
- The script logic and behavior remain identical
- The script passes with both `ash cf-ddns.sh` and `bash cf-ddns.sh`

## Full corrected script to use as the replacement

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# 切换到脚本所在目录
cd "$(dirname "$0")" || exit 1
# 设置 PATH 环境变量，确保系统能找到常用命令
export PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin

# 需要修改的部分
# 读取配置文件
CONFIG_FILE="$(dirname "$(realpath "$0")")/cf-config.ini"
if [ -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]; then
    . "$CONFIG_FILE"
else
    echo "Config file $CONFIG_FILE not found."
    exit 1
fi

# 日志函数，记录带时间戳的日志信息
log() {
    if [ -n "$1" ]; then
        printf "[%s] - %s\n" "$(date)" "$1" >> "$cloudflare_log"
    fi
}

# 检查必要变量是否为空
check_variables() {
    for var in auth_token zone_name record_name record_type cloudflare_log sender_email; do
        eval "val=\${$var}"
        if [ -z "$val" ]; then
            log "Error: $var is not set."
            exit 1
        fi
    done
    # 当 sender_email 为 1 时，检查 recipient_email
    if [ "$sender_email" = "1" ] && [ -z "$recipient_email" ]; then
        log "Error: recipient_email is not set while sender_email is true."
        exit 1
    fi
    # record_type 包含 A 时，检测 ipv4_file
    if echo " $record_type " | grep -q " A "; then
        if [ -z "$ipv4_file" ] && [ -z "$zone_identifier_v4_file" ]; then
            log "Error: ipv4_file or zone_identifier_v4_file is not set"
            exit 1
        fi
    fi
    # record_type 包含 AAAA 时，检测 ipv6_file
    if echo " $record_type " | grep -q " AAAA "; then
        if [ -z "$ipv6_file" ] && [ -z "$zone_identifier_v6_file" ]; then
            log "Error: ipv6_file or zone_identifier_v6_file is not set"
            exit 1
        fi
    fi
}

# 根据type A AAAA 判断 获取当前 IPv4 或 IPv6 地址
get_ip_address() {
    local type="$1"
    if [ "$type" = "A" ]; then
        local ip
        ip=$(curl --max-time 10 --retry 2 https://checkip.amazonaws.com)
        if [ -z "$ip" ]; then
            log "Failed to get IPv4 address (timeout or error)."
            exit 6
        fi
        echo "$ip"
    elif [ "$type" = "AAAA" ]; then
        local ip
        ip=$(ip route get 1:: | awk '{print $(NF-4);exit 1}')
        if [ -z "$ip" ]; then
            log "Failed to get IPv6 address from local network interfaces."
            exit 6
        fi
        echo "$ip"
    else
        log "Unknown type: $type"
        exit 5
    fi
}

# 检查 IP 地址是否变化（支持 IPv4/IPv6，参数1为新IP，参数2为类型A或AAAA）
check_ip_change() {
    local new_ip="$1"

body:
# Summary

Implement JSON configuration system and theming. The JSON configuration includes a JSON schema, markdown docs, and nix home manager support. Theming uses the same schema as configuration, but can be switched dynamically.

Theming makes use of color escapes sequences (OSC 21 or OSC 4,5,10-19,104,105,110-119) for querying the outer terminal's palette and setting the cursor and background colors. We also now support light/dark mode detection and palette change notifications. By default, ttx will automatically detect the terminal's color scheme via OSC 21/4 on start-up, and use that possibly match a theme. If no theme matches, we use ANSI colors. Users can also provide a theme in their configuration.

Also, our fzf menus now support previewing the selected item. This applies when changing themes, renaming tabs/sessions, and switching tabs/sessions.

Tab names will use OSC 0/2 or OSC 7 (cwd) by default if not explicitly named.

We also support rendering inactive panes dimmed, and by default dim the screen when a popup is present. This is configurable.

Closes #43, #15, #46

- [x] Update tests if necessary

Refactor AgentStreamer to use a queue-based __anext__ instead of wrapping

author: gabrielima7
body:
🛡️ Sentinel: [Medium] Fix PyJWT NotImplementedError Bypass in encode_jwt/decode_jwt

🚨 Severity: Medium
💡 Vulnerability: When encoding or decoding a JWT with an unsupported or random string provided for the `algorithm` argument, PyJWT raises a `NotImplementedError` rather than a `PyJWTError`. Because the TaipanStack `@safe_from` decorator did not explicitly catch `NotImplementedError`, it allowed the unhandled exception to bypass the `Result[T, E]` monad, leading to uncontrolled system crashes.
🎯 Impact: An attacker or system could trigger an application crash by injecting an invalid algorithm, bypassing intended system fault tolerance and error handling logic.
🔧 Fix: Explicitly added `NotImplementedError` to the `@safe_from` decorator's exception list for both `encode_jwt` and `decode_jwt`.
✅ Verification: Added a dedicated Hypothesis property-based test `test_fuzz_encode_jwt_malformed_algorithm` which bombards `encode_jwt` with invalid algorithm strings and verifies that it safely returns an `Err` result rather than crashing. All 1185 tests in the suite pass.

author: jylhis
body:
💡 **What:**
Optimized `jotain-utils-find-org-files-recursively` in `elisp/utils.el` by changing the `INCLUDE-DIRECTORIES` argument of `directory-files-recursively` to `nil`.

🎯 **Why:**
Previously, the recursive search returned both files and directories, which required a redundant `(file-regular-p file)` check inside the loop to filter out directories matching the `.org` extension. This triggered unnecessary OS-level `stat` system calls for every matched entry, creating a performance bottleneck when scanning systems with many nested directories.

📊 **Impact:**
Reduces I/O overhead by eliminating `stat` calls for `file-regular-p`. My local benchmarks show ~15-20% speedup in recursive directory lookups.

🔬 **Measurement:**
Tested and verified with Emacs Lisp benchmarking and ran tests to confirm functionality remains unchanged. Also ran the Nix code formatter to ensure style compliance.

author: benchoi93
body:
## Summary
- Replace `std::map<std::string, T*>` with `std::unordered_map` in 6 dictionary containers: `NamedObjectCont`, `MSEdge::DictType`, `MSLane::DictType`, `MSVehicleControl` vehicle/type dicts, `MSRoute::RouteDict`
- Replace `lower_bound`+`emplace_hint` insertion with `try_emplace`
- Add explicit sorting in `insertIDs()` for deterministic output order
- **Zero behavioral change** — all test scenarios produce identical output

## Motivation
Dictionary lookups via `std::map` use O(log n) string comparison. Replacing with `std::unordered_map` provides O(1) amortized lookups via hashing, improving TraCI query performance and network loading time by ~5-10% on large networks.

## Files Changed (7)

body:
Auto-dispatched task.

**Task:** TWO fixes on main branch in heartbeat.py and pipeline_runner.py:

1. CRITICAL: Move try/except INSIDE the completion processing loop in _beat() (heartbeat.py lines 99-104). Currently:
```
try:
    import pipeline_runner
    for completion in pipeline_runner.scan_for_completions():
        actions.extend(pipeline_runner.process_worker_completion(completion))
except Exception as e:
    actions.append(f'pipeline_runner error: {e}')

Change to:

import pipeline_runner
for completion in pipeline_runner.scan_for_completions():
    try:
        actions.extend(pipeline_runner.process_worker_completion(completion))
    except Exception as e:
        sid = completion.get('_session_id', 'unknown')

except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError):

except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError) as e:

## Summary
- Replace copy assignment of `myLFLinkLanesPrev` with `swap()`, eliminating a full vector copy per vehicle per action step
- Cache `getCarFollowModel()` as local `const MSCFModel&` in `executeMove()` and `processLinkApproaches()`, avoiding ~15 repeated pointer indirections per vehicle per step

`getCarFollowModel()` is an inline that dereferences `myType->myCarFollowModel`. Caching the reference once per function eliminates redundant pointer chasing in tight loops.

author: mssonicbld
body:
### why
vpp handles arp request internally and not punting it to control plane. SONiC needs to see arp request packet to create ip neighbour. Although vpp automatically create ip neighbour from arp internally, the neighbour is unknown to SONiC. This causes arp/test_arpall.py::test_arp_unicast_reply to fail because the test verifies if the neighbour is created in SONiC after peer sends arp request.

### what this PR does
1. register ethertype 0x0806 (arp) in linux-cp to punt arp to control plane
2. Implement add/remove ip neighbor over port channel interface. This was not implemented and it was relying on vpp creating ip neighbor internally. With the change of passing arp to control plane, it has to support creating ip neighbor through SAI

Signed-off-by: Sonic Build Admin <sonicbld@microsoft.com>

body: # What this PR does / why we need it: Closes #6173 Feature view versioning was introduced in #6101, but version-qualified feature references (e.g. `driver_stats@v2:trips_today`) only worked with the SQLite online store. All other online stores raised `VersionedOnlineReadNotSupported` when a versioned ref was used. This PR adds versioned read/write support to the FAISS online store, following the same pattern as the SQLite reference implementation: - **Write path**: when `enable_online_feature_view_versioning` is enabled, `_table_id` appends a `_v{N}` suffix to the in-memory key namespace (e.g. `project_driver_stats_v2`), routing materialization to the correct versioned index - **Read path**: version-qualified lookups (`@v2`) set `projection.version_tag` on the feature view before `online_read` is called; `_table_id` picks this up and routes to the correct index. `projection.version_tag` takes priority over `current_version_number` so explicit version requests are always honoured - **Multi-table support**: replaced single class-level `_index`/`_in_memory_store` with per-table `_indices`/`_in_memory_stores` dicts, so multiple feature views and versions can coexist in memory simultaneously - **Gate**: `_check_versioned_read_support` in `online_store.py` now allows `FaissOnlineStore` through All existing `online_read`, `online_write_batch`, `retrieve_online_documents`, `update`, and `teardown` methods are covered since every method resolves its namespace through `_table_id`. # Which issue(s) this PR fixes: Part of #2728 # Checks - [x] I've made sure the tests are passing. - [x] My commits are signed off (`git commit -s`) - [x] My PR title follows [conventional commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format ## Testing Strategy - [x] Unit tests - [ ] Integration tests - [ ] Manual tests - [ ] Testing is not required for this change Added 11 unit tests covering `_table_id` with versioning disabled, `projection.version_tag` priority over `current_version_number`, version 0 edge case, no version info fallback, versioned write/read round trips, namespace isolation between versions, missing index handling, and teardown cleanup. # Misc - Removed `"type"` from mock config in tests to match `FaissOnlineStoreConfig`'s strict pydantic validation (no extra fields permitted) ---

### Motivation
- Totals (over/under) probabilities were being modified by post-processing steps intended for non-totals markets, causing per-game totals sums to drift and producing invalid Over/Under pairs.

### Description
- Added a hard-preservation guard for totals at the top of `_align_moneyline_model_probability` so totals rows keep their existing `model_probability` during alignment.
- Reworked the non-moneyline fallback to apply a row-wise `_keep_totals_probability` that immediately returns the existing totals `model_probability` and only computes non-totals values when appropriate.
- Inserted a debug block that prints `[TOTALS AFTER ALIGN FIX]` and the per-`game_id` summed totals probabilities immediately after `_align_moneyline_model_probability` runs.
- After injury-adjusted `model_prob` is assigned to `model_probability`, added a totals-only normalization that groups by `game_id` and divides totals probabilities so each game’s totals sum to 1.0 before any non-totals clipping/adjustments.
- All changes are contained in `main.py` and target the post-processing pipeline that computes final `model_probability` and EVs.

### Testing
- Ran `python -m pytest -q sports_betting/tests/test_odds_mapping.py sports_betting/tests/test_totals_runtime_predictions.py`, but test collection failed with an import error (`ImportError: cannot import name 'UTC' from 'datetime'` under Python 3.10), so the tests could not execute.

author: copilot
body:
Preprocessing steps (non-finite filtering, sampling quality checks, variability checks, subsampling) lived inside `fit()` and `fit_LS()`, causing bugs where the GP trained on data that hadn't been cleaned at construction time. All such steps now run once at object creation.

## Changes

### `Lightcurve.__init__()` — new preprocessing parameters
- `max_samples` / `subsample_seed`: gap-preserving permanent subsampling on construction
- `check_sampling` / `sampling_kwargs`: per-band temporal quality check; bad bands are filtered from the stored data (2D) or raise `ValueError` (1D)
- `check_variability` / `variability_kwargs`: raises `ValueError` if the source is non-variable

Non-finite rows (NaN **and** Inf) are now always silently dropped before setting properties, regardless of the above flags.

```python
# Before: preprocessing was deferred to fit-time
lc = Lightcurve(t, y, yerr=ye)
lc.fit(model="2D", check_sampling=True, max_samples=3000, subsample_seed=42)

# After: data is validated and reduced at construction
lc = Lightcurve(t, y, yerr=ye,
                check_sampling=True,
                max_samples=3000, subsample_seed=42)
lc.fit(model="2D")
```

### `fit()` — simplified
- Removed `check_sampling`, `sampling_kwargs`, `check_variability`, `variability_kwargs`, `max_samples`, `subsample_seed` parameters
- Removed the `try/finally` block that temporarily swapped data buffers during subsampling

### `fit_LS()` — simplified
- Removed `max_samples` / `subsample_seed` parameters
- Removed the finite-value masking pass and subsampling loop (Steps 1 & 2); the method now reads `self.xdata`/`self.ydata`/`self.yerr` directly

### `_drop_nonfinite_rows()` — new static method
Replaces `_drop_nan_rows()` (kept as a deprecated shim) with `torch.isfinite()` so that both NaN and Inf are removed. Called unconditionally from `__init__()` for 1-D `ydata`.

### Tests
- `test_subsampling.py`: patterns using `lc.fit_LS(max_samples=N)` / `lc.fit(max_samples=N)` rewritten to `Lightcurve(..., max_samples=N)`; subsampling is now permanent, so tests that checked "original data restored" now verify data is permanently reduced
- `tests.py`: sampling-quality tests moved to `__init__()` context; `test_fit_band_filter_*` tests replaced with `test_init_band_filter_*` equivalents
- `test_best_band_init.py`, `test_mls_init.py`: removed `check_sampling=False` / `check_variability=False` from `fit()` kwargs

author: benchoi93
body:
## Summary
- Replace `myActiveLanes` from `std::list<MSLane*>` to `std::vector<MSLane*>` in `MSEdgeControl`
- Replace erase-in-loop with in-place compaction pattern in `planMovements()` and `executeMovements()`
- Remove early `break` in `changeLanes()` that depended on neighbors-first sorted ordering

## Motivation
The `std::list` erase-in-loop was the **dominant performance bottleneck** in SUMO's simulation loop. Each erase required pointer chasing through scattered heap nodes, and each iteration caused L1 cache misses on non-contiguous list nodes. These functions run every timestep on every active lane.

The vector compaction pattern (`writeIdx`) is O(n) with sequential memory access, dramatically improving cache locality.

## Benchmark Results
| Scenario | Before | After | Speedup |
|----------|--------|-------|---------|
| highway_corridor (5K veh, 3600s) | 74.2s | 10.3s | **7.2x** |
| insertion_heavy (10K veh) | 12.7s | 1.7s | **7.4x** |
| junction_priority (200 veh) | 0.70s | 0.07s | **10x** |
| lc_sublane_weave (100 veh, SL2015) | 9.3s | 2.4s | **3.9x** |
| **Total across 12 scenarios** | **~123s** | **~20s** | **~6x** |

## Behavioral Note
Removing the neighbors-first ordering and `break` optimization in `changeLanes()` may cause minor numerical differences (~0.01 m/s at individual timesteps) in some multi-lane scenarios due to changed lane processing order. In our testing, 8/10 component scenarios produced bit-identical FCD output; the remaining 2 showed differences well within SUMO's standard 1.01% floating-point tolerance. This is consistent with the existing tolerance used in TextTest comparisons.

## Files Changed (3)
- `src/microsim/MSEdgeControl.h` — `myActiveLanes` type change
- `src/microsim/MSEdgeControl.cpp` — compaction pattern in `planMovements()`, `executeMovements()`, `patchActiveLanes()`, `changeLanes()`
- `src/microsim/MSStateHandler.cpp` — `setActiveLanes()` parameter type

## Test plan
- [x] 10 component test scenarios pass (8 bit-identical, 2 within tolerance)
- [x] 2 integration test scenarios pass
- [x] Clean Release build, zero warnings
- [x] Verified with Krauss, IDM, EIDM, LC2013, SL2015 models

Signed-off-by: Seongjin Choi <benchoi93@gmail.com>

author: bstar16
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a modular, plan-driven synthetic placement primitive for the sweep-based build system that will become the standard placement primitive for future sweep execution.
- Keep the existing live build/placement path untouched and add this as parallel infrastructure to enable deterministic, schematic-driven placement in later phases.
- Capture placement outcomes in a typed, testable manner so sweep controllers can cleanly interpret placement results.

### Description
- Add a new `plan.sweep.air` subsystem containing `AirPlacementEngine`, `AirPlacementRequest`, and `AirPlacementOutcome` enums to represent typed placement results.
- Implement deterministic validation and mapping logic in `AirPlacementEngine` that performs request validation, held-item compatibility checks, explicit range checks, replaceability checks, synthetic `BlockHitResult` construction from neighbor faces, and mapping of interaction results to `AirPlacementOutcome` values (`SUCCESS`, `OUT_OF_RANGE`, `WRONG_ITEM`, `BLOCKED`, `FAILED_INTERACTION`, `INVALID_TARGET`).
- Expose isolated, static helpers (`validateRequest`, `classifyHeldItemCompatibility`, `isHeldItemCompatible`, `isWithinRange`, `mapInteractionResult`, `buildSyntheticHit`) so deterministic parts are easily unit-testable and independent of flight/crosshair or other runtime systems.
- Keep the implementation standalone and plan-driven (it does not depend on player crosshair aim or flight control) and does not replace the current active placement path.

### Testing
- Ran the focused unit test suite: `./gradlew test --tests com.example.mapart.plan.sweep.air.AirPlacementEngineTest` and it completed successfully.
- Tests cover wrong-item rejection, invalid-request rejection, out-of-range classification, deterministic interaction-result mapping, and request/outcome structure sanity and all passed.

📝 Description (รายละเอียด)
Pull Request นี้เป็นการเพิ่มและปรับปรุงระบบ Authentication (การลงทะเบียนและเข้าสู่ระบบ) แบบเต็มรูปแบบ โดยใช้ JWT (JSON Web Token) ที่เก็บผ่าน HTTP-Only Cookiesพร้อมทั้งปรับโครงสร้าง Environment Variables และแก้ไข Schema ของ Entity User ให้เหมาะสมกับการใช้งานมากขึ้น

🚀 Key Changes (การเปลี่ยนแปลงหลัก)
1. Authentication & API (ระบบล็อกอินและลงทะเบียน)

เพิ่ม Endpoint สำหรับ Login พร้อมตั้งค่าการสร้าง JWT Token
ปรับปรุง Logic สำหรับการ Registration พร้อมเพิ่ม Payload Validation เพื่อตรวจสอบความถูกต้องของข้อมูล

2. Security (ความปลอดภัย)

เปลี่ยนจากการส่ง Token ผ่าน Header/Body มาเป็นการใช้ HTTP-Only Cookies สำหรับเก็บ JWT
ตั้งค่า CORS ให้รองรับ Credentials (ให้สามารถรับส่ง Cookie ข้าม Origin ได้)
3. Database & Schema (ฐานข้อมูล)

body:
🎯 **What:** Implemented a `lex`/`yacc` timespec parser for the `at` utility, replacing the minimal ad-hoc string concatenation parser and fulfilling an actionable FIXME comment.
💡 **Why:** Parsing English time specifications (like "4:00 PM Jan 5" or "now + 2 hours") using standard C string functions manually is incredibly error-prone, hard to scale, and brittle. Leveraging standard tools like `lex` and `yacc` centralizes the parsing logic into a clean formal grammar, making the codebase much more maintainable and resilient.
✅ **Verification:** Verified by building `usr.bin/lex` and `usr.bin/yacc` natively and using them to generate the lexer and parser. Successfully compiled `lib/at` with the new artifacts and ran internal test suites.
✨ **Result:** A robust, standard-compliant lex/yacc parser is now available for general timespecs in the `at` library.

## 💡 Change Scope

- [ ] **Small Change**
- [x] **Large Change**

## 📝 What Does This PR Do?

Implements Phase 4 (M1–M4) “Remote Worker + Web UI (SSH-first)” v0:

- Extract reusable Control Surface HTTP server (`POST /invoke`, bearer token auth, connection file)
- Add headless Node worker entry (`out/main/worker.js`) running the same contracts/handlers
- Add minimal built-in web shell served by the worker (`GET /`) for quick debug / manual invoke
- CLI: support `--endpoint` + `--token` for tunnels/remote + `opencove worker start/status`
- Docs: add SSH-first tunnel workflow
- Tests: worker web shell contract coverage + web UI (non-Electron) behavior differences

---

## 🏗️ Large Change Spec

**1. Context & Business Logic**

- Goal: move Control Surface from Desktop-only to Worker-first without changing contracts, enabling SSH-tunneled remote execution.
- Transport remains HTTP (`/invoke`) with the same `{ kind, id, payload }` contract shape.

**2. State Ownership & Invariants**

- Owner: Worker owns side effects + durable truth when used (filesystem/worktree/pty/persistence).
- Invariant: contracts/envelope are transport-agnostic and unchanged.
- Invariant: guardrails do not regress (approved roots remain required for filesystem/worktree actions).
- Invariant: default security is conservative (bind `127.0.0.1` + bearer token; remote via `ssh -L`).

**3. Verification Plan & Regression Layer**

- `pnpm pre-commit` (tsc + lint/format checks + vitest + playwright e2e) ✅
- Contract tests (Node env): Control Surface HTTP server + web shell (`GET /`, token auth, invalid JSON)
- Unit tests (happy-dom): web UI differences for space path actions (clipboard fallback; openers unavailable)

body:
## Summary
- Rewrite `ZstdTokenEncoder` to accumulate compressed output in a single `MAX_DATA_COUNT` buffer, matching upstream `token.c:send_zstd_token()` lines 733-769
- Previously wrote multiple small DEFLATED_DATA blocks per token; now writes one buffer-full block per fill/flush, matching upstream's single-buffer pattern
- Add `output_pos` field tracking buffer write position (matches upstream `zstd_out_buff.pos`)
- Replace multi-piece `write_deflated_output` with single-buffer `write_output_buffer`
- Add upstream source line references throughout encoder and decoder
- Add 8 new tests covering flush boundaries, wire ordering, MAX_DATA_COUNT splitting, reset, and golden byte header

## Test plan
- [ ] CI passes (fmt, clippy, nextest on all platforms)
- [ ] Existing zstd roundtrip tests still pass
- [ ] New tests verify single DEFLATED_DATA block output for small input
- [ ] Zstd interop with upstream rsync 3.4.1 (via interop CI)

author: shkiper2006
body:
### Motivation
- Enable saving transcription notes directly to Google Workspace (Docs or Sheets) using per-user Google OAuth credentials. 
- Persist user Google tokens and per-user mode so sync can be performed reliably and optionally refreshed.
- Provide a simple, deployable integration without adding heavy 3rd-party clients by calling Google REST endpoints.

### Description
- Implemented real OAuth code->token exchange and refresh against `https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token` with scopes for Docs and Sheets in `GoogleOAuthService` (`app/google/oauth.py`).
- Added user fields `google_notes_mode`, `google_access_token`, `google_refresh_token`, and `google_token_expires_at` to `User` model plus Alembic migration `alembic/versions/20260330_0002_google_credentials.py` to persist them.
- Added `GoogleDocsService` (`app/google/docs_service.py`) which appends timestamped entries in format `[YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS] text`, and `GoogleSheetsService` (`app/google/sheets_service.py`) which appends rows (`Date`, `Time`, `Text`).
- Added `GoogleNoteSyncService` (`app/google/note_sync_service.py`) that chooses mode from per-user setting or env fallback, refreshes access token when expired, and delegates to Docs/Sheets services.
- Wired transcription pipeline to call the Google sync after generating the summary note and save a fact-note about sync success/failure in `notes` (`app/tasks/transcription.py`).
- Extended API: `/auth/google/callback` now persists tokens for a provided `telegram_user_id` and a new endpoint `/users/{telegram_user_id}/google-mode` sets per-user mode (`docs|sheets`) (`app/api/routes.py`).

### Testing
- Ran `python -m compileall app` and verified the project modules compile successfully.
- Ran `pytest -q`, which failed to import due to missing environment dependency (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'sqlalchemy'`) so unit tests could not be executed in this environment.
- Verified code load/compile and basic behavior via local static checks and manual inspection of new files and migration.

author: jackie-jiaqi-yin
body:
## Summary
- auto-discover GitHub repo and PR context from the local checkout instead of treating a PR URL as a normal required input
- collect the current-branch PR when available, plus repo-level open PRs and recent closed PRs for notebook context
- surface PR resolution details in the analysis brief and run manifest, and update the notebook docs/prompts to match the new default behavior

## Why
The notebook workflow still centered the explicit GitHub PR URL even though the local repo already exposes enough information to resolve GitHub context automatically. That made first runs noisier than necessary and dropped useful historical context when the relevant experiment work lived in recently closed PRs rather than the current branch.

## Impact
Users can run `experiment-results-notebook` from a normal local checkout without supplying a repo link or PR number, while still getting richer GitHub context in the generated notebook artifacts.

## Validation
- `python -m py_compile experiment-results-notebook/scripts/*.py`
- smoke-tested `fetch_github_context` against this repo; it resolved `jackie-jiaqi-yin/codex-skills` from local git state, selected the current-branch PR source path, and collected recent closed PR context

author: emeroad
body:
This pull request introduces a new batch-based gRPC Span sender to the agent, allowing Spans to be sent in batches via a unary RPC, as an alternative to the existing streaming approach. The batch sender is configurable and disabled by default. The main changes include new configuration options, supporting code to read and apply these options, and the provider for the new batch sender.

**Key changes:**

### Configuration and Properties

* Added new configuration options for the Span batch sender (such as enable flag, batch size, flush interval, deadline, and max concurrent requests) to `pinpoint-root.config` and profile-specific configs, with the batch sender disabled by default. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-20ae8b0977ce97a7e5f506eca7b7231a570a51523ac9b7b88d231d7bf26ebabcR130-R138) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1b874666a72b9059afa192ca19941ffc67c6e4db212614ca09958b5ba3adadcfR24-R25) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-7b980b4ee645cc825e2ae038ae3cb6e040ba1c93bc1e558badc95ad6686f96c7R24-R25)

### Core Implementation

* Introduced the `SpanBatchSenderConfig` class to encapsulate batch sender settings, including default values and property bindings.
* Updated `GrpcTransportConfig` to include, read, and expose the `SpanBatchSenderConfig` for use throughout the agent. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-974f5ea4460780d8db8840d043b5b9b265637831b8befdf29a6906b23dcf7037R158-R159) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-974f5ea4460780d8db8840d043b5b9b265637831b8befdf29a6906b23dcf7037R194-R196) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-974f5ea4460780d8db8840d043b5b9b265637831b8befdf29a6906b23dcf7037R217-R223) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-974f5ea4460780d8db8840d043b5b9b265637831b8befdf29a6906b23dcf7037R428-R431) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-974f5ea4460780d8db8840d043b5b9b265637831b8befdf29a6906b23dcf7037R470)

### Dependency Injection and Sender Selection

* Modified `GrpcModule` to select between the standard and batch span sender providers based on the new configuration, and to bind the new batch sender provider when enabled. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-87bf61e282d59e8e1f4f8c57355b1d4a851e882029421abf59f52c1d3a7b3228R39) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-87bf61e282d59e8e1f4f8c57355b1d4a851e882029421abf59f52c1d3a7b3228R61) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-87bf61e282d59e8e1f4f8c57355b1d4a851e882029421abf59f52c1d3a7b3228L127-R129) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-87bf61e282d59e8e1f4f8c57355b1d4a851e882029421abf59f52c1d3a7b3228L197-R199) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-87bf61e282d59e8e1f4f8c57355b1d4a851e882029421abf59f52c1d3a7b3228R214-R221)

### New Batch Sender Provider

* Added the `SpanBatchGrpcDataSenderProvider` class, which constructs and provides the batch-based gRPC Span sender, wiring up all necessary dependencies and configuration.

These changes lay the groundwork for more efficient Span transmission and provide flexibility for future performance tuning and feature enablement.

author: ekkoitac
body:
## Fix Issue #3849: launchctl FileNotFoundError on macOS with UV Python

When hermes is installed via UV on macOS, UV's bundled Python ships with a minimal PATH that excludes `/bin` and `/usr/bin`. Since `gateway.py` calls `subprocess.run(["launchctl", ...])` without an absolute path, it fails with `FileNotFoundError`.

**Fix:** Replace hardcoded `"launchctl"` with `shutil.which("launchctl") or "/usr/sbin/launchctl"` so the binary is found regardless of PATH.

```python
# Before
subprocess.run(["launchctl", "load", str(plist_path)])

# After
subprocess.run([shutil.which("launchctl") or "/usr/sbin/launchctl", "load", str(plist_path)])
```

author: stevendufresne
body:
Part of DOTMSD-1187

## Proposed Changes

- Rename the `/me/profile` route to `/me/account` across the Dashboard client
- Rename the exported route from `profileRoute` to `accountRoute`
- Rename the `Profile` page component to `Account`
- Rename the `me/profile/` directory to `me/account/`
- Update all internal links and references to use `/me/account`
- Update classic Calypso's secondary menu import to alias the renamed export
- Add a `/me/profile` → `/me/account` redirect in the Dashboard router

## Approach

We rename the route path from `/profile` to `/account` unconditionally, treating `/me/account` as the canonical path going forward. However, user-facing labels ("Profile" vs "Account") are handled based on the `dashboard/omnibar` feature flag:

- **When omnibar is off** (current production): Labels that appear in the old UI (secondary menu dropdown, header me-menu, page title) continue to say "Profile" so nothing looks different to users today.
- **When omnibar is on** (new dashboard): Labels say "Account" to match the new navigation design.

This is opinionated — it assumes we will land on "Account" as the final label once the omnibar ships. By changing the route path now, we avoid a future migration. The only thing gated behind the feature flag is the display text in legacy UI, not the underlying route.

A legacy redirect from `/me/profile` to `/me/account` is included so existing bookmarks and links continue to work.

## Testing Instructions

**With omnibar off:**
1. Navigate to `/me` — verify it redirects to `/me/account`
2. Navigate to `/me/profile` — verify it redirects to `/me/account`
3. The header menu should show "Profile" as the first item
4. The sidebar should show "Account" as the first item
5. The page title should say "Profile"
6. The account dropdown in the secondary menu should show "Profile"

**With omnibar on:**
1. Navigate to `/me` — verify it redirects to `/me/account`
2. Navigate to `/me/profile` — verify it redirects to `/me/account`
3. The sidebar should show "Account" as the first item
4. The page title should say "Account"

## Pre-merge Checklist

- [ ] Has the general commit checklist been followed? (PCYsg-hS-p2)
- [ ] [Have you written new tests](https://wpcalypso.wordpress.com/devdocs/docs/testing/index.md) for your changes?
- [ ] Have you tested the feature in Simple (P9HQHe-k8-p2), Atomic (P9HQHe-jW-p2), and self-hosted Jetpack sites (PCYsg-g6b-p2)?
- [ ] Have you checked for TypeScript, React or other console errors?
- [ ] Have you tested accessibility for your changes? Ensure the feature remains usable with various user agents (e.g., browsers), interfaces (e.g., keyboard navigation), and assistive technologies (e.g., screen readers) (PCYsg-S3g-p2).
- [ ] Have you used memoizing on expensive computations? More info in [Memoizing with create-selector](https://github.com/Automattic/wp-calypso/blob/trunk/packages/state-utils/src/create-selector/README.md) and [Using memoizing selectors](https://react-redux.js.org/api/hooks#using-memoizing-selectors) and [Our Approach to Data](https://github.com/Automattic/wp-calypso/blob/trunk/docs/our-approach-to-data.md)

    - [ ] For UI changes, have we tested the change in various languages (for example, ES, PT, FR, or DE)? The length of text and words vary significantly between languages.

body:
Severity: Medium
Vulnerability: Swallowed errors (empty catch blocks) hide command execution failures and mask underlying issues.
Impact: Diagnosability is reduced. Upstream calls may proceed in undefined states if command execution failed silently.
Fix: Created a centralized `reporter.ReportError` package and funneled all ignored `_ = err` blocks in `v4/lib/exec.go` through it.
Verification: Ran `go build ./...` successfully and ensured no functionality was regressed.

Assumptions: The project wants to log these errors using the standard `log` package, as no existing centralized logger was found.
Alternatives Not Chosen: Adding a Sentry integration was out of scope. Passing the error up the stack changes the function signature, which may break other consumers.
How To Pivot: Remove `v4/lib/internal/reporter/reporter.go` and revert `v4/lib/exec.go` to use `_ = err` again.
Next Knobs: `v4/lib/internal/reporter/reporter.go` can be updated to use a custom logger (e.g. `logrus`, `zap`, or Sentry) without touching the call sites.

---

- Prevent regressions in daily report wording, section semantics and table-based formatting by locking current outputs with deterministic snapshot tests.
- Make the state-model explicit in docs so future changes do not reintroduce bugs where simulated/recommended fields are mistaken for executed account state.

### Description

Current Portfolio Overview (Executed / Real State)`, `B. Recommended Actions Today (Recommended / Not Executed)`, and `C. Hypothetical Target Allocation (Simulated / Recommended)`.

### [`v1.12.3`](https://redirect.github.com/lib/pq/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v1123-2026-04-03)

- Treat io.ErrUnexpectedEOF as driver.ErrBadConn so database/sql discards the

  especially with CockroachDB which frequently sends partial messages ([#​1299]).

[#​1299]: https://redirect.github.com/lib/pq/pull/1299

### [`v1.12.1`](https://redirect.github.com/lib/pq/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v1121-2026-03-30)

- Look for pgpass file in \~/.pgpass instead of \~/.postgresql/pgpass ([#​1300]).

- Don't clear password if directly set on pq.Config ([#​1302]).

[#​1300]: https://redirect.github.com/lib/pq/pull/1300

[#​1302]: https://redirect.github.com/lib/pq/pull/1302

### [`v1.12.0`](https://redirect.github.com/lib/pq/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v1120-2026-03-18)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/lib/pq/compare/v1.11.2...v1.12.0)

- The next release may change the default sslmode from `require` to `prefer`.
  See [#​1271] for details.

- `CopyIn()` and `CopyInToSchema()` have been marked as deprecated. These are
  simple query builders and not needed for `COPY [..] FROM STDIN` support (which
  is *not* deprecated). ([#​1279])

  ```
  // Old
  tx.Prepare(CopyIn("temp", "num", "text", "blob", "nothing"))

  // Replacement
  tx.Prepare(`copy temp (num, text, blob, nothing) from stdin`)
  ```

##### Features

- Support protocol 3.2, and the `min_protocol_version` and
  `max_protocol_version` DSN parameters ([#​1258]).

- Support `sslmode=prefer` and `sslmode=allow` ([#​1270]).

- Support `ssl_min_protocol_version` and `ssl_max_protocol_version` ([#​1277]).

- Support connection service file to load connection details ([#​1285]).

- Support `sslrootcert=system` and use `~/.postgresql/root.crt` as the default
  value of sslrootcert ([#​1280], [#​1281]).

- Add a new `pqerror` package with PostgreSQL error codes ([#​1275]).

  For example, to test if an error is a UNIQUE constraint violation:

  ```
  if pqErr, ok := errors.AsType[*pq.Error](err); ok && pqErr.Code == pqerror.UniqueViolation {
      log.Fatalf("email %q already exsts", email)
  }
  ```

  To make this a bit more convenient, it also adds a `pq.As()` function:

  ```
  pqErr := pq.As(err, pqerror.UniqueViolation)
  if pqErr != nil {
      log.Fatalf("email %q already exsts", email)
  }
  ```

##### Fixes

- Fix SSL key permission check to allow modes stricter than [0600/0640#1265](https://redirect.github.com/0600/0640/issues/1265) ([#​1265]).

- Fix Hstore to work with binary parameters ([#​1278]).

- Clearer error when starting a new query while pq is still processing another
  query ([#​1272]).

- Send intermediate CAs with client certificates, so they can be signed by an
  intermediate CA ([#​1267]).

- Use `time.UTC` for UTC aliases such as `Etc/UTC` ([#​1282]).

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/lib/pq/compare/v1.11.1...v1.11.2)

This fixes two regressions:

- Don't send startup parameters if there is no value, improving compatibility
  with Supavisor ([#​1260]).

- Don't send `dbname` as a startup parameter if `database=[..]` is used in the
  connection string. It's recommended to use dbname=, as database= is not a
  libpq option, and only worked by accident previously. ([#​1261])

[#​1260]: https://redirect.github.com/lib/pq/pull/1260

[#​1261]: https://redirect.github.com/lib/pq/pull/1261

### [`v1.11.1`](https://redirect.github.com/lib/pq/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v1111-2026-01-29)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/lib/pq/compare/v1.11.0...v1.11.1)

This fixes two regressions present in the v1.11.0 release:

- Fix build on 32bit systems, Windows, and Plan 9 ([#​1253]).

- Named \[]byte types and pointers to \[]byte (e.g. `*[]byte`, `json.RawMessage`)
  would be treated as an array instead of bytea ([#​1252]).

[#​1252]: https://redirect.github.com/lib/pq/pull/1252

[#​1253]: https://redirect.github.com/lib/pq/pull/1253

### [`v1.11.0`](https://redirect.github.com/lib/pq/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#v1110-2026-01-28)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/lib/pq/compare/v1.10.9...v1.11.0)

This version of pq requires Go 1.21 or newer.

pq now supports only maintained PostgreSQL releases, which is PostgreSQL 14 and
newer. Previously PostgreSQL 8.4 and newer were supported.

##### Features

- The `pq.Error.Error()` text  includes the position of the error (if reported
  by PostgreSQL) and SQLSTATE code ([#​1219], [#​1224]):

  ```
  pq: column "columndoesntexist" does not exist at column 8 (42703)
  pq: syntax error at or near ")" at position 2:71 (42601)
  ```

- The `pq.Error.ErrorWithDetail()` method prints a more detailed multiline
  message, with the Detail, Hint, and error position (if any) ([#​1219]):

  ```
  ERROR:   syntax error at or near ")" (42601)
  CONTEXT: line 12, column 1:

       10 |     name           varchar,
       11 |     version        varchar,
       12 | );
            ^
  ```

- Add `Config`, `NewConfig()`, and `NewConnectorConfig()` to supply connection
  details in a more structured way ([#​1240]).

- Support `hostaddr` and `$PGHOSTADDR` ([#​1243]).

- Support multiple values in `host`, `port`, and `hostaddr`, which are each
  tried in order, or randomly if `load_balance_hosts=random` is set ([#​1246]).

- Support `target_session_attrs` connection parameter ([#​1246]).

- Support [`sslnegotiation`] to use SSL without negotiation ([#​1180]).

- Allow using a custom `tls.Config`, for example for encrypted keys ([#​1228])
